title: Graphs
subtitle: Model relationships as vertices and edges, then choose a frontier or ordering whose invariant matches the question.
variables: V = number of vertices, E = number of input edges (undirected adjacency stores 2E entries), R*C = grid cells, K = number of states per vertex, W = maximum edge weight, Q = queries; S = number of supplied BFS sources. Unless specified, vertices are integer IDs 0..V-1 and adjacency endpoints are valid; inputs are not mutated. Adjacency-list traversal is O(V+E), matrix traversal O(V²). Hash-table costs are expected; long string labels cost O(label length) to hash initially and compare in the worst case, so map to integer IDs for repeated work. Python integers are arbitrary precision: stated arithmetic bounds use a unit-cost bounded-word model. Auxiliary space includes stacks/queues and algorithm state, excludes input and separately identified output. Heap bounds refer to lazy heapq implementations and count duplicate entries. H = heap size; B = allowed edge budget for bounded relaxation. heapq sift work is logarithmic, but CPython list resize can make a single heap operation linear; sequence bounds use amortization. Exact path-count DP may hold exponentially large integers; modulus bounds bit costs. Hash expectations are not adversarial guarantees: many colliding keys can make a lookup linear in table size. For empty strings an O(L) walk means O(1+L) including fixed call/root work. Python list append/pop may resize linearly on a single call; amortized bounds apply over sequences.

templateDetails.preconditions: Unweighted directed or undirected adjacency lists, valid integer endpoints. Returns complete distance array (-1 unreachable) and any shortest source→target vertex path; source==target gives [source]. No input mutation. Empty graph has no valid source and raises ValueError.
templateDetails.observation: Distance is fixed on first enqueue, not on arbitrary first encounter.

templateDetails.preconditions: Symmetric unweighted undirected adjacency lists with valid IDs. Returns (number of components, component label for each vertex), including isolated vertices; []→(0,[]). Parallel edges/self-loops allowed; no mutation. Not SCC for directed input.
templateDetails.observation: An outer loop accounts for isolates without adding special edge cases.

templateDetails.preconditions: Grid entries 0=open, nonzero=wall, four-direction moves. S integer-coordinate source pairs consumed once; duplicate sources ignored. Returns nearest-source edge distances, -1 for walls/unreachable. Empty shapes supported if sources empty; bad shape/source raises ValueError. Input unchanged.
templateDetails.observation: One shared frontier computes distance to the nearest of all sources.

templateDetails.preconditions: Directed integer-ID adjacency; None is not a vertex ID. Returns bool, []→False. Iterator frames preserve the actual active ancestor chain without recursion. Input unchanged; parallel forward edges do not by themselves form a cycle.
templateDetails.observation: The suspended iterator makes GRAY exactly the active ancestor chain.

templateDetails.preconditions: Directed valid-ID adjacency; edges prerequisite→dependent. Returns one topological order, None on a cycle, [] for no vertices. Parallel edges counted consistently. No mutation; queue order is not lexicographically minimal.
templateDetails.observation: Queue exhaustion is not success unless every vertex was removed.

templateDetails.preconditions: Symmetric undirected adjacency, valid IDs. Returns 0/1 colors, None when impossible (including self-loop), [] on empty. For one-way inequality constraints first symmetrize edges. Does not mutate input.
templateDetails.observation: An odd cycle forces a same-color edge somewhere, even in a disconnected component.

templateDetails.preconditions: Weighted directed or symmetric undirected adjacency as (neighbor, nonnegative finite numeric weight). Integer IDs make heap ties orderable. Returns distances, infinity for unreachable. No mutation; invalid source, endpoint or negative weight raises ValueError. For arbitrary node objects add an itertools.count tie-breaker.
templateDetails.observation: Only a current minimum pop settles a nonnegative distance.

templateDetails.preconditions: Weighted directed or symmetric undirected adjacency; weights exactly 0/1. Returns distances with infinity unreachable. Checks source/endpoints/weights; no mutation. A first-enqueue visited flag would incorrectly suppress later zero-cost improvement.
templateDetails.observation: Zero improvements belong before pending unit-cost layers.

templateDetails.preconditions: n vertices; reusable sequence edges of directed (u,v,finite numeric weight); negative edges allowed. Returns finite shortest distances or infinity unreachable, but rejects any source-reachable negative cycle instead of returning partially invalid answers. Unreachable negative cycles ignored. No mutation. For a stop budget use a copied next-round array, not this in-place unbounded-path variant.
templateDetails.observation: V−1 passes suffice for simple paths; one extra reachable improvement signals a bad cycle.

templateDetails.preconditions: Weighted directed DAG with valid integer endpoints and finite numeric weights, including negative ones. Rejects cycles anywhere, even unreachable components. Returns distance array; infinity for unreachable. No mutation; O(V+E) without a heap.
templateDetails.observation: A topological order settles incoming dependencies even when edge weights are negative.

templateDetails.preconditions: Directed edge iterable, finite numeric weights; add both directions for undirected input. Parallel edges use minimum weight; empty n=0 returns []. Any negative cycle anywhere raises ValueError rather than exposing invalid pair distances. No input mutation; negative undirected edges necessarily produce a negative closed walk.
templateDetails.observation: The intermediate vertex loop must be outermost.

templateDetails.preconditions: Symmetric undirected weighted adjacency, valid integer endpoints and finite numeric weights; negative weights/parallel edges allowed. Returns MST total, None if disconnected, 0 for empty or singleton. Self-loops ignored. Does not return chosen edges or mutate input; do not apply to directed graphs.
templateDetails.observation: Prim accepts the cheapest crossing edge, not a shortest source path.

templateDetails.preconditions: Directed valid integer-ID adjacency. Returns (SCC count, component label per vertex), []→(0,[]). Equal labels iff mutually reachable. Labels need not match another implementation’s numbering. True iterator-frame finishing order is essential; no recursion or input mutation.
templateDetails.observation: True exit order, then reverse-graph traversal, isolates mutually reachable groups.

templateDetails.preconditions: Undirected edge iterable, valid n and endpoints checked. Returns input edge IDs whose removal increases component count, in DFS exit order (not sorted). Handles self-loops, parallel edges, disconnected and empty graphs. No recursion/mutation; IDs refer to enumerate(edges), so retain input if endpoint output is desired.
templateDetails.observation: Skip one parent edge ID, not every neighbor equal to the parent.

templateDetails.preconditions: Rectangular 0/1 grid, four directions, k nonnegative integer eliminations. Returns shortest edge count from top-left to bottom-right or -1, including empty grid. Entering a 1 costs one elimination, including starting cell. Input unchanged. Cap K=min(k,RC): a shortest feasible route can be simple, so more than RC eliminations cannot improve feasibility. State retains remaining budget; copy to adapt for keys or parity.
templateDetails.observation: A cell and its remaining budget together determine future choices.

templateDetails.preconditions: Directed valid-ID adjacency; returns sorted IDs from which every path eventually terminates. Parallel edges counted individually, self-loops unsafe, [] returns []. Does not mutate input. Nodes merely able to reach one terminal may still be unsafe.
templateDetails.observation: Universal eventual safety means every outgoing successor is already safe.

templateDetails.preconditions: Directed finite numeric edge weights, possibly negative; B=max_edges≥0. Returns cheapest walk using at most B edges (not unrestricted shortest paths); bounded negative cycles are well-defined. Each round reads only the previous snapshot. A K-stop flight permits K+1 edges. Copies edge iterable; no caller mutation. O(BV) copying matters, so not simply O(BE).
templateDetails.observation: Reading old distances prevents spending several edges in one budget round.

templateDetails.preconditions: Rectangular finite numeric heights, four directions. Returns minimum possible largest adjacent absolute difference, 0 on singleton and None for empty shapes. No input mutation. Monotone max-extension, not additive relaxation, justifies settling; negative heights themselves are fine.
templateDetails.observation: A bottleneck extends by max, not addition.

templateDetails.preconditions: Finite numeric coordinate pairs; implicit complete undirected graph with Manhattan weights. Returns MST total (0 on empty/singleton); duplicates produce valid zero edges. No input mutation or quadratic edge storage. Dense array scan beats heap overhead for this representation.
templateDetails.observation: Complete implicit graphs can avoid storing a quadratic edge set.

templateDetails.preconditions: Directed DAG with valid integer IDs; returns number of source-to-each-vertex paths, counting the empty source path once and parallel edges as distinct choices. Rejects any cycle, including unreachable ones. No mutation; optional positive modulus bounds count sizes. Without modulus path counts may be exponential in value, so integer bit time/storage exceed unit-cost O(V+E)/O(V).
templateDetails.observation: Counting paths does not require enumerating them; exact counts may have many bits.

templateDetails.preconditions: Reachable graph of GraphNode objects with default identity hashing/equality, directed or symmetric undirected neighbor lists. None returns None. Allocates a structurally independent clone of reachable nodes and neighbor lists; values are shared references, not deep-copied payloads. Preserves neighbor order, parallel edges and self-loops. Distinct original nodes may share equal values and must remain distinct. No original mutation; custom value-based equality requires an identity-keyed adaptation.
templateDetails.observation: Memoize a new clone before following its edges, so cycles terminate and repeated references stay shared.

decisionProcess: 0–25 seconds — Define vertices and legal edges: directed or undirected, explicit lists/matrix or implicit moves, full state identity, parallel edges and self-loops. Ask boolean, distance, one path, count or all paths.
25–50 seconds — If only reachability/components, choose iterative DFS/BFS; directed mutual reachability means SCC. If prerequisites, choose Kahn/active-DFS, and DAG DP only after proving acyclicity.

50–85 seconds — For shortest paths inspect weights: equal→BFS; 0/1→0–1 BFS; nonnegative→Dijkstra; DAG even with negatives→topological relaxation; other negatives→Bellman–Ford. A bounded edge budget needs snapshots; all-pairs small V may justify Floyd.

85–110 seconds — Change state/frontier when required: simultaneous sources seed together; keys/budgets/masks enlarge identity; minimax costs use max relaxation. A cheap network connecting all vertices is MST, not shortest path.

110–145 seconds — State invariant and reject the tempting wrong tool: visited does not mean active, first Dijkstra insertion does not settle, position-only seen is unsafe with resources. Estimate V,E and expanded states before coding.

145–180 seconds — Quote representation + validation + frontier + output/bit costs; decide mutation/tie policy and iterative depth strategy. Trace empty/isolated/self-loop plus one algorithm-specific adversary (diamond, negative edge, parallel bridge or threshold tie).
